restoration_note: Teaching describes the Five Sons / garments of the First Man weeping three times at descent (foreknowing the Darkness, then silent under Necessity) and a fourth, unending weeping at the consummation when souls 'prepared for the Error' are separated from the Last Andrias and bound with the Darkness they loved. Restorations were strongly constrained by: (a) visible partial traces in restoration-type gaps, (b) parallel phrasing across lines (ⲱⲁⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ, ⲥⲱⲭⲡ̄ ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ, ⲡⲁⲛⲇⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ ⲛⲁⲃⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈), (c) standard Lycopolitan idioms (ⲕⲱ ⲡⲟⲩϩⲟ ϩⲁⲧⲏ⸗, ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ), (d) the lexicon entries for Last Andrias, Darkness, Error, souls. Gaps 24-26 are pure lacunae in a damaged passage describing what the firmaments stand hidden before; the residual partial letters do not yield enough constraint to choose among possible nouns and were left unrestored.

restorations.basis: Editor restoration completing ⲡⲥⲁⲡ 'the time/moment'; only final ⲡ missing.
Editor restoration; ⲁⲗⲗⲁ opens the contrastive clause continued by ⲁⲗⲗⲁ … in the next phrase. Fits the spiritual arc: foresight of suffering BUT they entered under Necessity.
Editor restoration completing ⲁⲣⲁϩ/ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'unto him' (the King of Darkness foreseen as Enemy).
Editor restoration; ⲙⲓϣⲉ 'fight/engage' completes 'they hastened in unto him' under Necessity — the cosmogonic engagement of the First Man's sons against the Darkness foreseen.
Standard Lyc demonstrative referring back to ⲡⲥⲁⲡ 'the time/chosen moment'; only ⲙⲙⲉⲩ visible.
Standard directional with ⲃⲱⲕ; the Last Andrias 'goes up' as the gathering-statue rising at the consummation. Idiom ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ is a fixed lexicon expression for ascent.
Conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ- + ⲕⲁⲁⲩ; only ⲛ̄ⲥ bracketed. Fits the spiritual reading: the Andrias goes up and leaves the unredeemed behind.
Standard ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧ⸗ 'alone' with 3pl suffix; expresses the souls left isolated after the Andrias rises.
ⲥⲱϫⲡ̄ 'remain, be left behind' — verb explicitly used at line 24 (ⲥⲱⲭⲡ̄ ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ) for the eschatological remnant; only ⲡ bracketed.
Completes idiom ⲥⲱⲭⲡ̄ ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'be left behind forever' — exact phrase recurs in line 24.
Verb ⲱⲁⲧ 'cut off' parallels lines 23 (ⲱⲁⲁⲧⲟⲩ) and 33 (ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲱⲁⲧⲟⲩ); the eschatological severance from the Last Andrias.
3pl object suffix completing ⲱⲁⲧⲟⲩ from gap 10.
Lyc ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲓϩⲉ-style demonstrative phrase; partial ⲉⲓ̈ⲧ visible, completion -ⲩ in next line.
Final ⲩ of ⲛⲧⲉⲓⲧⲟⲩ continuing from previous line.
Greek loan κατά governing 'recompense of works' — fits doctrine of correspondence-retribution by works; only ⲕⲁⲧ bracketed.
Standard ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ ⲁ- 'into', continuing into ⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'Darkness' in next line — those who 'enter into the Darkness' to be bound with it.
Lexicon term ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'Darkness' — the destination of those bound by their loves; only ⲕⲉⲕ bracketed.
Perfect 3pl ⲁⲩ-; only ⲩ bracketed. Subject prefix for 'they loved it'.
Standard idiom ⲕⲱ ⲡⲟⲩϩⲟ ϩⲁⲧⲏ⸗ 'set their face toward'; lexicon entry ⲡⲍⲟ='face' (state expressed outward) — they orient their state toward the Darkness.
Reduplicated ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'hour by hour, continually' — describes the persistent loving-of-Darkness that fixes the soul's correspondence.
Demonstrative referring to the chosen moment; parallel to gap 4. Only ⲧⲙ̄ bracketed.
Directional, parallel to gap 5 — the Last Andrias goes up at the consummation.
ϩⲛ̄ + 3sg.f suffix referring back to ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ ('chosen moment', often f.) or to ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ; only ⲧⲥ̄ bracketed.
Future + verb ⲣⲓⲙⲉ 'weep' — central verb of the chapter; only ⲉⲛ bracketed.

2-char lacuna between ⲛ and ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁϩⲉ; insufficient context to choose between possible noun-stems or demonstrative + relative ('of those who stand'). The grammatical referent (firmaments-of-elements) does not fit the 2-char slot, and no parallel formula constrains the fill.

3-char lacuna after ⲙ in 'before the souls and m___ of n___ who are prepared for the Error'. Multiple plausible candidates (ⲙⲉⲗⲏ 'members', ⲙⲣⲣⲉ 'bonds', ⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'thoughts') with no decisive parallel; mark unrestorable.
2-char lacuna after ⲛ̄ depending on gap 25. Cannot be constrained without resolving the previous gap.
Future circumstantial introducing the contrast 'they shall weep, but in that weeping they shall not be silenced'; only ⲛⲁ bracketed.
Demonstrative + ordinal-prefix beginning ⲡⲓⲙⲁϩϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the fourth' — completes 'theirs is not the [fourth] weeping' contrast across the line break.
Lyc ⲡⲓⲙⲁϩϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the fourth' completing ordinal across line break from gap 28. Central to chapter's structure of three+one weepings.
Standard plural ⲯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ; the firmaments grieve over the souls 'who shall be cut off from the rest' (continuation in next line names exactly these); only ⲉ bracketed.
